units.translation: - 306 ⟦1⟧ (⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧ 332) recalls the ⟦4⟧ (defixiones) on lead tablets buried or hung up in sanctuaries of the underworld gods, Plat. ⟦5⟧. ⟦6⟧, 933 A (Weckl.): ⟦7⟧, and see the collection of tablets found in Athens in the appendix to the C. I. Att.: Defixionum tabellae Atticae ed. R. Wünsch, where ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ (⟦10⟧), especially with regard to speaking, is carried out.
by sorceries and incantations and binding spells
the hands and the feet and the tongue and the soul

As often elsewhere, anapests precede the stationary song, during which the chorus takes up the position suitable for the stationary song; so here too the anapest has the character of a marching rhythm.

According to the tradition there are 6 systems, of 3, 2, 3, 2, 2, 3 verses; but the 3rd system must be supplemented by one anapest or emended so that the paroemiac disappears; I prefer the latter, according to which 5 systems of 3, 2, 4, 2, 3 verses remain. Regularity in the verse numbers is not necessary, see on ⟦1⟧ – ⟦2⟧ as ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧;

⟦1⟧ appellatively (often Euripides, Ddf.) also ⟦2⟧. ⟦3⟧ in A. wavers between the Attic and the Ionic inflection; for ⟦4⟧ the Attic would be ⟦5⟧ (so ⟦6⟧), and this active perfect occurs only here at all.

⟦1⟧ according to the Schol. are the lots of men; on the other hand, according to V. 334. 347. 386 it seems to mean the lot (office) assigned to the Erinyes over men. However, ⟦2⟧ is so clearly "allots", and the parallel ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧ so exact, that I follow the Schol. Also the elaboration in 312 ff. connects better in this way, and "how we administer our portion among men" would be rather meaningless. Below 930 ⟦5⟧; 953 ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧ (= ⟦9⟧).
for these obtained by lot to manage all things among men
and they accomplish openly and completely the affairs of men
but to others a life dimmed by tears
and a stranger allots the lots of steel
The following verses are disfigured by numerous small corruptions, which can, however, be removed.
